page: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 10 physical cores and 20 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 160.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes 1181 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, but does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory workloads, with notable strengths in specific compression tasks. The single-threaded gzip compression speed reaches 35.47 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at 14.71 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 20081.26, while the PassMark CPU score is 33317.5. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show read speeds of 141.96 GB/sec and write speeds of 58.49 GB/sec. For database operations, the server handles 34.81 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database score of 10336.74.

The hardware configuration offers high memory density relative to compute resources, which provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. However, the 10 physical cores may limit highly parallelized compute tasks compared to compute-optimized instances. The presence of Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) supports specialized vector and matrix operations, as reflected in the small-model LLM inference prompt processing speed of 2009.7 tokens per second. This server is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data compression pipelines, and moderate-scale language model inference.
